enquiry: Our research group is evaluating a spectral measurement interface using model biological tissues such as chicken muscle, fat and liver. We want to compare MIR ATR and fluorescence information, because the material is heterogeneous and sequential measurements may not sample the same location. This is a laboratory classification study. We need a first comparison experiment and a clear statement of what its results would demonstrate.

clarification_questions.question: What classification decision should the first experiment support, and what goes wrong with the current approach to tissue identification?
clarification_questions.why: Defines what the comparison must demonstrate and whether the study is aimed at method selection or a specific application.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Purpose is a general method comparison on model tissues; the first experiment is exploratory.

clarification_questions.question: Which tissue classes must be distinguished (for example muscle, fat, liver), and is any specific component or fluorescent species of interest?
clarification_questions.why: Determines the classification task and whether fluorescence can measure a defined species at all.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Target classes are the three stated tissues; no specific analyte or fluorophore is defined, so lab screening must establish whether fluorescence carries a usable signal.

clarification_questions.question: How will the tissue samples be presented (fresh or frozen, cut or whole, surface condition), and is the surface opaque or otherwise optically variable?
clarification_questions.why: Sets whether ATR contact is reproducible and how the optical signal varies between samples.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Samples are opaque solid tissue with variable surface; ATR contact reproducibility is to be verified in lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: How is sample handling controlled (storage, time from excision to measurement, temperature, cleaning between samples), and how does tissue composition vary within a sample?
clarification_questions.why: Heterogeneity and handling change both spectra and fluorescence; the design must control or record them.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Handling is not controlled; the design records time and temperature per sample and treats within-sample variation as a source of error.

clarification_questions.question: What is the interface design (probe type, fiber type, combi-probe or separate probes) and how are the MIR-ATR and fluorescence measurements aligned to the same spot?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether the same location is sampled, the central requirement of the stated comparison.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Interface type is unknown; the design requires a same-spot arrangement, verified before any comparison.

clarification_questions.question: What reference method or ground truth defines tissue identity for each sample, and what accuracy does it have?
clarification_questions.why: Without an independent reference, classification performance cannot be judged.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: No reference method is defined; tissue identity is assumed from sample labelling and must be verified before the comparison is judged.

clarification_questions.question: What classification accuracy and response time would count as a useful result, and what is the planned number of independent sample batches for validation?
clarification_questions.why: Sets the acceptance criteria the comparison is judged against.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: No acceptance criteria are defined; the experiment reports performance with uncertainty and is judged on the single-method baseline first.

clarification_questions.question: Is the study research only, or is a later clinical, medical or industrial use planned?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether results from in-vitro model tissues may be interpreted beyond the laboratory.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Research only; results from model tissues are not evidence for clinical or industrial use.

flags_before_revision.detail: not_supported: The cited DOCX §3 is the assistant brief. It warns against citing lab studies as proof of clinical readiness, but it does not state that lab results show signal quality and class separation on model tissue. The claim attributes a factual finding to a page that only gives guidance. Fix: Attribute the lab-results point to S04 p.4 and S04 p.3, and keep the readiness caveat as a general guidance statement tied to the brief.

not_supported: S04 p.3 attributes the broad fat-sample standard deviation to tissue inhomogeneity, with spectra mixing lipids and proteins. It does not mention contact variation, and it does not say either factor can mimic class differences. Fix: Limit the risk to tissue inhomogeneity, citing S04 p.3, and state contact variation as an assumption to test rather than a sourced finding.

RAMAN.nominal_range: Raman shift in cm-1; signal recorded in the visible / short-wave NIR (400-1100 nm); state the laser excitation separately [S01 p.11]

FLUO.nominal_range: UV/Vis excitation and emission; depends on the fluorescent species [S01 p.12]

UVVIS.nominal_range: UV 190-360 nm and visible; depends on target and setup [S01 p.5]

rule_hints: fluorescence_needs_fluorophore: Fluorescence only measures a defined fluorescent species or a justified indicator; most chemicals do not fluoresce. [S01 p.5; S04 p.4; DOCX §5]
sensitivity_not_selectivity: High sensitivity does not imply selectivity. Fluorimetry and UV/Vis are rated high sensitivity but low selectivity. [S01 Table 1 (p.6); DOCX §5]
nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]
combination_is_hypothesis: Combining methods can add complementary information, but the gain is a hypothesis to test against the best single method. [S01 p.7-8; DOCX §5]

fiber_limits_wavelength: The fiber determines which wavelengths reach the probe. Silica fibers transmit up to about 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR; mid-IR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers. [S02 p.6; S04 p.1; DOCX §5]
remote_measurement_nir_silica: NIR works with standard glass optics and silica fibers, which suits remote online measurement; robust silica cables of 100-300 m exist. [S01 p.5; S02 p.7]
same_spot_for_heterogeneous: For heterogeneous or fast-changing samples, methods should measure the same spot at the same time, e.g. with a combi probe. [S01 p.8; S04 p.2]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
insufficient_information_is_valid: If the known facts cannot justify a method choice, say so, ask the deciding questions and propose the next step. [DOCX §3]
